message.content:
You are black-box reverse-engineering a compiled Python program so it can be reimplemented in pure JavaScript.

The program is: /workspace/dataset/test9_executable
Its source is exactly:

    import yaml, argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), explicit_start=True)
    print(result)

HARD RULES
- NEVER run `python`/`python3`. Only run the executable. It bundles its own deps.
- You may NOT read PyYAML source (it is not on disk). Everything must come from observed behavior.
- Do not write anything into /output.
- To pass multi-line / tricky values safely, write the value's exact bytes to a file and run:
    node -e 'const{spawnSync}=require("child_process");const fs=require("fs");const a=fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8");const r=spawnSync("/workspace/dataset/test9_executable",["--a",a],{encoding:"utf8"});process.stdout.write("RC="+r.status+"\n---stdout---\n"+r.stdout+"---end---\n"+(r.status?r.stderr.split("\n").slice(-6).join("\n"):""))' /path/to/case.txt
  Piping the output through `cat -A` (or using od -c) is essential for whitespace-exact observation.

DELIVERABLES (both required)
1. A dense, implementation-ready spec at /workspace/dev/spec/<AREA>.md
   - Exact byte-level observations. Tables of input -> exact output. Quote whitespace explicitly (use  markers like <SP>, <TAB>, <NL> where ambiguous).
   - State the inferred RULE behind each observation, and the boundary you probed to pin it down (e.g. "wraps at column 81, verified with 79/80/81/82-char values").
   - Flag anything you could NOT pin down as an OPEN QUESTION with what you tried.
2. Differential test cases: one file per case at /workspace/dev/cases/<AREA>/<nn>-<slug>.txt containing the RAW bytes of the --a value (a trailing newline in the file IS part of the value; omit it if the value has none). Aim for 40-90 well-chosen cases in your area: normal, boundary, and adversarial. These will be replayed against both implementations byte-for-byte, so favor cases that discriminate between plausible implementations.
   Write case files with node/fs (or printf) so the bytes are exact. Verify each case actually runs the way you expect before keeping it. Do NOT keep a case whose observed behavior you did not record in the spec.

Your final message must be a compact summary of the RULES you established (not a list of files) — the most surprising/non-obvious findings first, at most 60 lines. Another engineer will implement from your spec file, but your summary is what the orchestrator reads.


AREA: YAML input syntax — scanning and parsing (what shapes of input parse, and into what structure).
Cover exhaustively: block mappings and sequences; nested/indentation rules; indentless sequences under a mapping key; flow mappings/sequences ({} [] with nesting, trailing commas, empty entries, missing values like {a: , b}); flow scalars inside flow context; ': ' vs ':' rules (plain scalars containing colons, "a:b" vs "a: b", colon before ] or }); '#' comments (start of line, after value, inside quotes, '#' needing a preceding space); plain scalar termination and multi-line plain scalars (folding, leading/trailing space stripping, empty-line folding); single-quoted scalars ('' escape, multi-line folding); double-quoted scalars (ALL \ escapes: \0 \a \b \t \n \v \f \r \e \" \\ \N \_ \L \P \xXX \uXXXX \UXXXXXXXX, \<newline> line continuation, folding, escaped whitespace at line end, invalid escapes); block scalars | and > with all header combos (|, |-, |+, |2, |-2, |2-, >, >-, >+, > with more-indented lines, leading blank lines, tabs, trailing newlines, chomping semantics); anchors & aliases (&a, *a, on keys, on nested nodes, aliasing a collection so the SAME object is referenced twice, self-referencing/recursive anchors); tags (!!str !!int !!map !!seq !!binary etc, verbatim !<tag>, unknown tag -> error, !local tag -> error?); document markers ('---' with a value on the same line, leading '---', '...' end marker, TWO documents -> what error/exit code, '---' alone, empty input, input that is only comments/whitespace); directives (%YAML 1.1, %YAML 1.2 -> what changes?, %YAML 2.0 -> warning?, %TAG); explicit keys ('? key' / ': value', '?' with a collection key, '? a' with no value); simple-key limits (a very long plain key >1024 chars in flow, a key spanning lines -> error); tabs in various positions; CR / CRLF / \x85 / U+2028 line breaks in the input; BOM; NUL and other non-printables -> error text.
Record the resulting Python structure indirectly, via the dumped output.

Use AREA = "scanner-parser" for your file paths: spec at /workspace/dev/spec/scanner-parser.md, cases in /workspace/dev/cases/scanner-parser/.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# AREA: scanner-parser — YAML input syntax accepted by `test9_executable`

Program: `/workspace/dataset/test9_executable`
Equivalent to `print(yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(argv_a), explicit_start=True))`
(PyYAML 6.x, `SafeLoader` for input; **`yaml.Dumper` (not SafeDumper) for output**).

Everything below is from black-box observation. Case files live in
`/workspace/dev/cases/scanner-parser/`; the raw replay log used to write this
spec is `/workspace/dev/_sp/rec.txt` (regenerate with
`node /workspace/dev/_sp/record.js`).

Notation: `<SP>`/`·` = space, `<TAB>`, `<NL>` = LF, `<CR>`, `<NEL>` = U+0085,
`<LS>` = U+2028, `<PS>` = U+2029, `<BOM>` = U+FEFF, `<NBSP>` = U+00A0.

---

## 0. Harness / process-level facts (read first)

| fact | detail |
|---|---|
| success | exit code **0**, result on stdout, stderr empty |
| any YAML error | exit code **1**, **stdout empty**, Python traceback on stderr |
| stderr last line | `[PYI-<n>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test9' due to unhandled exception!` where `<n>` **varies run to run** → stderr is *not* byte-reproducible. Only RC + stdout are. |
| `print()` | adds one extra `<NL>` after `yaml.dump`'s output, so every successful stdout ends with `\n\n` (dump already ends with `\n`) |
| argparse quirk | the value is passed as `["--a", value]`. `argparse` treats a token as an option if it starts with `-` **and contains no ASCII space**. So `---`, `----`, `-`, `-\n-\n-\n` → **RC=2**, `usage: ...` + `error: argument --a: expected one argument`. Values that start with `-` but contain a space (e.g. `- 1\n- 2`, `--- foo`) are fine. |
| NUL | `\x00` cannot be passed through `argv` at all (OS/execve limit). Untestable — **OPEN QUESTION** (see §12). |

Error-message shape (when you want to reproduce stderr text, ignore the PYI line):

```
yaml.<module>.<Class>Error: <context>            <- optional context line
  in "<unicode string>", line L, column C:
    <snippet of that line>
    <caret>
<problem>                                        <- always present
  in "<unicode string>", line L2, column C2:
    <snippet>
    <caret>
```
`line`/`column` are **1-based**. Snippets are indented 4 spaces and elided with
` ... ` when the line is long (see case 99/100). `ReaderError` uses
`in "<unicode string>", position N` with a **0-based codepoint index** instead.

---

## 1. Reader layer (runs BEFORE any scanning) — printability + line breaks

### 1.1 Printability check (whole input, up-front)
The entire string is scanned once at load time. First character outside
`\x09 \x0A \x0D \x20-\x7E \x85 \xA0-퟿ -� \U00010000-\U0010FFFF`
raises immediately, before any token is produced:

```
yaml.reader.ReaderError: unacceptable character #x00XX: special characters are not allowed
  in "<unicode string>", position N
```
`#x00XX` = lowercase hex, min 4 digits (`#x0001`, `#x000b`, `#x007f`, `#x009f`, `#xfffe`).
`N` = 0-based codepoint offset of the offending char.

Verified boundaries: `\x01` ✗, `\x09` ✓, `\x0B` ✗, `\x0C` ✗, `\x0D` ✓, `\x7E` ✓,
`\x7F` ✗, `\x84` ✗, `\x85` ✓, `\x9F` ✗, `\xA0` ✓, `�` ✓, `￾` ✗.
Note the asymmetry: `\v`/`\f` are legal **escapes** inside `"…"` but the raw
bytes `\x0B`/`\x0C` are rejected by the reader.

### 1.2 Line breaks
`\n`, `\r\n`, `\r`, `\x85` are all line breaks and are **normalised to `\n`**.
` ` and ` ` are line breaks too (they end lines, reset column,
increment the line counter) but `scan_line_break` returns the **character
itself**, so they survive into scalar values verbatim.

| input | value |
|---|---|
| `a: 1<CR><NL>b: 2<CR><NL>` | `{a: 1, b: 2}` |
| `a: 1<CR>b: 2<CR>` | `{a: 1, b: 2}` |
| `a: 1<NEL>b: x<NEL>··y<NL>` | `{a: 1, b: "x y"}` — NEL folds like `\n` |
| `a: x<LS>··y<NL>` | `{a: "x y"}` — **not** folded to a space |
| `b: p<PS>··q<NL>` | `{b: "p q"}` |
| `a: \|<LS>··x<LS>··y<LS>` | `{a: "x y "}` — literal block keeps LS as-is |

### 1.3 BOM
* A `<BOM>` at **index 0 only** is skipped (once, in `scan_to_next_token`).
* A `<BOM>` anywhere else is an ordinary character and becomes part of the token
  (`a: 1<NL><BOM>b: 2` → keys `a` and `"﻿b"`).
* `<BOM>` **does not advance the column counter**. So `a:<NL>·<BOM>·b: 1` has
  its key token at column 1 (not 2) and the key text is `"﻿ b"` (dumped at
  indent 2 as `··"﻿·b": 1`). Case 109.

---

## 2. Whitespace: TABS ARE ALMOST ALWAYS AN ERROR

`scan_to_next_token` skips **only `' '`**. Consequently a `<TAB>` at any position
where a *token* could start is fatal:

```
yaml.scanner.ScannerError: while scanning for the next token
found character '\t' that cannot start any token
```

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `a:<TAB>b` | ERROR at line 1 col 3 |
| `a: b<TAB>c` | ERROR at line 1 col 5 (plain scalar ends at the TAB) |
| `a: 1<TAB><NL>` | ERROR at col 5 (trailing TAB!) |
| `a: 1·<TAB># c` | ERROR at col 6 |
| `<TAB>a: 1` / `a:<NL><TAB>b: 1` / `a:<NL>·<TAB>b: 1` | ERROR (TAB can never be indentation) |
| `[a,<TAB>b]` / `{a: 1,<TAB>b: 2}` | ERROR |
| `a:<NL>  x<NL><TAB><NL>  y` (TAB-only line inside a literal block) | ERROR — the block scalar ends at the un-indented TAB line |

TABs are legal **inside** scalar content: single-quoted, double-quoted, and
block-scalar bodies (after the indentation has been stripped).
`a: 'x<TAB>y'`, `b: "p<TAB>q"`, `c: \|<NL>··x<TAB>y<NL>··<TAB>z<NL>`
→ `{a: "x\ty", b: "p\tq", c: "x\ty\n\tz\n"}` (case 102).

---

## 3. Simple keys (`allow_simple_key` state machine)

A plain/quoted scalar can be a mapping key only if a *simple key* is currently
allowed. Track a boolean `allowSimpleKey`, plus a per-flow-level saved
"possible simple key" record `{index, line, column, required}`.

`allowSimpleKey` transitions:

| event | new value |
|---|---|
| stream start | `true` |
| line break consumed while `flowLevel == 0` | `true` |
| `%directive` | `false` |
| `---` or `...` token | `false` |
| `[` or `{` | `true` (and a possible simple key is saved for the outer level first) |
| `]` or `}` | `false` |
| `,` | `true` |
| `-` (block entry) | `true` |
| `?` (key indicator) | `!flowLevel` |
| `:` (value indicator) | `false` |
| `&anchor`, `*alias`, `!tag` | `false` |
| `\|`/`>` block scalar | `true` |
| `'…'` / `"…"` | `false` |
| plain scalar | `false` |

Fatal checks:
* `-` at block level while `!allowSimpleKey` → `ScannerError: sequence entries are not allowed here`
* `?` at block level while `!allowSimpleKey` → `ScannerError: mapping keys are not allowed here`
* `:` with no pending simple key, block level, `!allowSimpleKey` → `ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here`

This single rule explains a large family of errors:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `--- foo` | OK → scalar document |
| `--- {a: 1}` / `--- [1,2]` | OK |
| `--- a: 1` | **ERROR** `mapping values are not allowed here` (1:6) |
| `--- - a` | **ERROR** `sequence entries are not allowed here` (1:5) |
| `--- \|<NL>  x`, `--- &a 1`, `--- !!str 1`, `--- 'x'` | OK |
| `key: a: b` | ERROR `mapping values are not allowed here` (1:7) |
| `a: b:` (colon at EOL) | ERROR (1:5) |
| `a: :` | ERROR (1:4) |
| `a: - x` | ERROR `sequence entries are not allowed here` (1:4) |
| `a: ?` | ERROR `mapping keys are not allowed here` (1:4) |
| `: b` | ERROR `ParserError: while parsing a block mapping / expected <block end>, but found ':'` (1:1) |

### 3.1 Simple-key staleness → the 1024 limit and the one-line limit
A saved possible simple key is discarded when `key.line != currentLine` **or**
`currentIndex - key.index > 1024`. If the discarded key was `required`
(`required = (flowLevel == 0 && scannerIndent == key.column)`), discarding
raises instead:

```
yaml.scanner.ScannerError: while scanning a simple key
  in "<unicode string>", line <keyline>, column <keycol>:
could not find expected ':'
  in "<unicode string>", line <eofline>, column 1:
```

Boundaries pinned:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `k`×1024 + `: v` (block) | **OK** → `? <key><NL>: v` |
| `k`×1025 + `: v` (block) | ERROR `mapping values are not allowed here` at col 1026 |
| `{` + `k`×1024 + `: v}` | **OK** (`key.index` is 1, so span = 1024) |
| `{` + `k`×1030 + `: v}` | ERROR `expected ',' or '}', but got ':'` at col 1032 |
| `"` + `k`×1030 + `": v` | ERROR (span counts the quotes) |
| `a<NL>b: 1` (key spanning 2 lines) | ERROR `mapping values are not allowed here` (2:2) |
| `"a<NL>b": 1` | ERROR (2:3) |
| `a:<NL>1<NL>` | ERROR `while scanning a simple key … could not find expected ':'` — `1` sits at column 0 == block indent → *required* key |
| `a:<NL>  b: one<NL>  two<NL>` | same "required key" error: `two` at column 2 == the inner map's indent |
| `a: one<NL>---- x<NL>` | same error: `---- x` is a plain scalar at column 0 == indent |

Contrast: `a: one<NL>  # c<NL>  two<NL>` → the comment terminates the plain
scalar; `two` is at column 2 but the enclosing map's indent is 0, so the key is
*not* required → the **parser** complains instead:
`ParserError: while parsing a block mapping / expected <block end>, but found '<scalar>'` (3:3).

---

## 4. Block mappings, block sequences, indentation

* A block mapping/sequence's indent is the column of its first key / first `-`.
* Deeper-indented content at the *same* logical level → `ScannerError: mapping
  values are not allowed here` (the key's `:` is rejected).
* Shallower-but-unmatched indent → `ParserError: expected <block end>, but found …`.

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `a: 1<NL>b: two<NL>` | `{a: 1, b: two}` |
| `a:<NL>  b: 1<NL>  c: 2<NL>` | nested map |
| `a:<NL>- 1<NL>- 2<NL>` | **indentless sequence allowed**: `{a: [1,2]}` |
| `a:<NL>  - 1<NL>  - 2<NL>` | same value |
| `a:<NL>- b:<NL>  - c<NL>` | `{a: [{b: [c]}]}` |
| `a:<NL>  b:<NL>  - 1<NL>` | `{a: {b: [1]}}` (indentless seq under a nested key) |
| `a:<NL>  b:<NL>- 1<NL>` | ERROR `expected <block end>, but found '-'` (3:1) — an indentless sequence may only be indentless w.r.t. **its own** parent key, not an outer one |
| `- a: 1<NL>   b: 2<NL>` | ERROR `mapping values are not allowed here` (2:5) |
| `a:<NL>  b: 1<NL>   c: 2<NL>` | ERROR `mapping values are not allowed here` (3:5) |
| `a:<NL>   b: 1<NL>  c: 2<NL>` | ERROR `expected <block end>, but found '<block mapping start>'` (3:3) |
| `- a: 1<NL>  b: 2<NL>- c: 3<NL>` | `[{a:1,b:2},{c:3}]` (compact map in seq item) |
| `- - - deep` | `[[[deep]]]` |
| `a:<NL>  1<NL>` | `{a: 1}` (value on the next line) |
| `a:<NL>b:<NL>` | `{a: null, b: null}` |
| `-<NL>- a<NL>` | `[null, a]` |
| `-<NL>  - <NL>    - x<NL>` | `[[[x]]]` |
| blank lines anywhere between entries | ignored |

---

## 5. Flow collections

* `flowLevel` increments on `[`/`{`. Indentation is irrelevant inside flow
  (a flow collection may start at col 4 and continue at col 0).
* `,` may trail: `[1, 2, ]`, `{a: 1, }`, `[[1,],[2,],]` all fine.
* An **empty entry between commas is an error**: `[1, , 2]` →
  `ParserError: while parsing a flow node / expected the node content, but found ','` (1:5).
  Same for `[,]` and `{,}`.
* A flow mapping entry may omit the value: `{a: , b, c: 1, d:}` →
  `{a: null, b: null, c: 1, d: null}`.
* A flow *sequence* entry may be a single-pair mapping: `[a: 1, b:, c:d]` →
  `[{a:1},{b:null},"c:d"]`; `[? a]` → `[{a: null}]`.
* `?` is accepted in flow mappings: `{? a: b, ? c, d: e}` → `{a:b, c:null, d:e}`.
* `{: v}` → ERROR `expected the node content, but found ':'`.
* Block indicators are illegal in flow: `[- a]` → `expected the node content,
  but found '-'`; `[\|<NL> x]` → `ScannerError: found character '\|' that cannot
  start any token`.
* Unclosed → `ParserError: while parsing a flow sequence/mapping … expected
  ',' or ']'/'}' , but got '<stream end>'`.
* Mismatched bracket `a: [1}` → `expected ',' or ']', but got '}'`.
* Extra closer `a: [1]]` → `expected <block end>, but found ']'`.
* Comments and newlines are allowed inside flow: `{a: 1, # c<NL> b: 2}` OK.
* Nesting depth is not limited in practice (200-deep `[[[…1…]]]` works).
* Unhashable keys (collection used as a mapping key, in flow or via `? …`) →
  `ConstructorError: … found unhashable key`.

---

## 6. `:` and plain-scalar termination

### 6.1 Where `:` ends a plain scalar
A `:` inside a plain scalar terminates it iff the **next** character is
`\0`, `<SP>`, `<TAB>`, or a line break — **plus**, when `flowLevel > 0`, also
one of `, [ ] { }`.

### 6.2 Extra flow-only terminators
When `flowLevel > 0` a plain scalar also ends at any of `, ? [ ] { }`.

| input | value |
|---|---|
| `key: a:b` | `{key: "a:b"}` |
| `k2: :b` | `{k2: ":b"}` |
| `k3: b:,c` | `{k3: "b:,c"}` (block: `,` is ordinary, `:` followed by `,` is ordinary) |
| `a:: 1` | `{"a:": 1}` |
| `a   :   b` | `{a: b}` (spaces before `:` are dropped with the key's trailing spaces) |
| `y w : c` | `{"y w": c}` |
| `[a:b]` | `["a:b"]` (`:` followed by `b`) |
| `[a:]` | `[{a: null}]` (`:` followed by `]` → terminator in flow) |
| `[a:,b]` | `[{a: null}, "b"]` |
| `{a:b: 1}` | `{"a:b": 1}` |
| `{a: b:}` | ERROR `expected ',' or '}', but got ':'` |
| `[a: 1: 2]` | ERROR `expected ',' or ']', but got ':'` (1:6) |
| `[a?b]`, `[a ? b]` | ERROR `expected ',' or ']', but got '?'` |
| `[a{b]` | ERROR `… but got '{'` |
| `[x]y]` | `[x]` then junk → `ParserError: expected '<document start>', but found '<scalar>'` |

### 6.3 Characters that cannot START a plain scalar
`,` `[` `]` `{` `}` → `ParserError: while parsing a block node / expected the
node content, but found '<c>'`.
`@` `` ` `` `%` → `ScannerError: while scanning for the next token / found
character '<c>' that cannot start any token`.
`&`/`*`/`!`/`\|`/`>`/`'`/`"`/`?<SP>`/`-<SP>`/`:<SP>` are read as their own
indicators (see the relevant sections). All of these characters are fine
*inside* a plain scalar: `x,y`, `x]y`, `x}y`, `x&y`, `x*y`, `x!y`, `x\|y`, `x>y`,
`x'y`, `x"y`, `-x`, `?x`, `x-y`, `?a` (as key) all parse as plain text.

### 6.4 Spaces in plain scalars
Internal runs of spaces are preserved **verbatim** (never collapsed):
`a: x   y` → `"x   y"`. Trailing spaces before EOL/EOF are dropped:
`a: x   <NL>` → `"x"`.

### 6.5 Multi-line plain scalars (folding)
A plain scalar continues on the next line iff (block context) the continuation
column `>= scannerIndent + 1`, where `scannerIndent` is the current block
indent (`-1` at document root → continuation may start at column 0).

Folding: one line break → one `<SP>`; *n* additional blank lines → *n* `\n`
(the space is suppressed). Trailing spaces on the earlier line and leading
spaces on the continuation line are dropped.

| input | value |
|---|---|
| `a: one<NL>  two<NL>  three` | `"one two three"` |
| `a: one   <NL>  two` | `"one two"` |
| `a: one<NL>     two` | `"one two"` |
| `a: one<NL><NL>  two` | `"one\ntwo"` |
| `a: one<NL><NL><NL>  two` | `"one\n\ntwo"` |
| `one<NL>two<NL>three<NL>` (document root) | `"one two three"` |
| `a:<NL>  b: one<NL>   two` | `{a:{b:"one two"}}` (col 3 ≥ 2+1) |
| `a:<NL>  b: one<NL>  two` | ERROR (col 2 < 3) → required-simple-key error |
| `a: one<NL>two: 3` | `{a: "one", two: 3}` (col 0 < 1 → scalar ends) |
| `a: x<LS>  y` | `"x y"` (LS/PS breaks are inserted literally, not folded) |

A plain scalar also stops at a line whose first 3 chars are `---` or `...`
**followed by space/break/EOF**, at column 0:
`a: one<NL>...<NL>` → `{a: one}` + document end (OK);
`a: one<NL>--- x<NL>` → `ComposerError … but found another document`;
`a: one<NL>  ...<NL>` → indented → folds → `"one ..."`;
`a: one<NL>---- x` → not a marker (4th char is `-`) → plain scalar `---- x` at
col 0 → required-simple-key error.

---

## 7. Comments

* `#` starts a comment when it appears where a token could start, i.e. at the
  beginning of a line (after optional spaces) **or** after at least one space.
* `#` **not** preceded by a space is ordinary plain-scalar text.
* Comments are ignored entirely (never attached to the output).

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `a: b#c` | `{a: "b#c"}` |
| `a: b #c` | `{a: b}` |
| `a#b: 1` | `{"a#b": 1}` |
| `a: #c` | `{a: null}` |
| `#c: 1` | whole line is a comment → document is `null` |
| `# a<NL># b<NL>` | `null` |
| `#<NL>` | `null` |
| `a: 1<NL>    # c<NL>b: 2` | `{a:1,b:2}` (comment indentation irrelevant) |
| `a:<NL>  # c1<NL>  # c2<NL>  1` | `{a: 1}` |
| `- # c<NL>  a` | `[a]` |
| `[1, # c<NL> 2]` | `[1,2]` |
| `a: "b#c"` / `a: 'b # c'` | `#` inside quotes is literal |
| `a: 1 #` (no text, no NL) | `{a: 1}` |
| `a: one<NL>  # c<NL>  two` | **ERROR** — comment terminates the plain scalar (see §3.1) |
| `a: \|<NL>  # not comment<NL>` | `{a: "# not comment\n"}` — no comments inside block scalars |
| `a: 1 <TAB># c` | ERROR (TAB, §2) |

---

## 8. Quoted scalars

### 8.1 Single quoted
`''` is the only escape → one `'`. Backslashes are literal (`'a\nb'` → `a\nb`).
Folding identical to plain scalars (break → space; *n* blank lines → *n* `\n`;
surrounding spaces trimmed). Tabs allowed. Unterminated →
`ScannerError: while scanning a quoted scalar / found unexpected end of stream`.

### 8.2 Double quoted — complete escape table
| escape | produces | escape | produces |
|---|---|---|---|
| `\0` | U+0000 | `\"` | `"` |
| `\a` | U+0007 | `\\` | `\` |
| `\b` | U+0008 | `\/` | `/` |
| `\t` | U+0009 | `\<SP>` | space |
| `\<TAB>` (literal TAB after `\`) | U+0009 | `\N` | U+0085 |
| `\n` | U+000A | `\_` | U+00A0 |
| `\v` | U+000B | `\L` | U+2028 |
| `\f` | U+000C | `\P` | U+2029 |
| `\r` | U+000D | `\xHH` | 2 hex digits |
| `\e` | U+001B | `\uHHHH` | 4 hex digits |
| | | `\UHHHHHHHH` | 8 hex digits |

* Unknown escape → `ScannerError: while scanning a double-quoted scalar /
  found unknown escape character 'q'` (column points at the escape char).
* Bad/short hex → `expected escape sequence of N hexadecimal numbers, but found
  '<c>'` (N = 2/4/8).
* `\<NL>` = line continuation: the break **and** the leading whitespace of the
  next line are dropped; whitespace *before* the `\` is kept.
  `"x\<NL>  y"` → `"xy"`; `"x \<NL>  y"` → `"x y"`.
* Unescaped folding is the same as single-quoted:
  `"x<NL>  y"` → `"x y"`; `"x<NL><NL>  y"` → `"x\ny"`;
  `"x   <NL>  y"` → `"x y"`; `"x<NL>   <NL>  y"` → `"x\ny"`;
  `"x<NL><TAB>y"` → `"x y"` (leading TAB on the continuation line is stripped).
* Unterminated → `found unexpected end of stream`.

### 8.3 Empty / whitespace values
`a: ""` → `''`; `b: "   "` → `'   '`; `c: ''` → `''`.
An **empty string key** is legal: `"": 1` → mapping `{"": 1}`.

---

## 9. Block scalars `|` and `>`

Header grammar: `('|'|'>') ( [+-] [1-9]? | [1-9]? [+-]? ) ( <SP>* comment )? <NL>`
Both orders work (`|2-` and `|-2`). Errors:

| header | error (`ScannerError: while scanning a block scalar`) |
|---|---|
| `\|0` | `expected indentation indicator in the range 1-9, but found 0` (col of `0`) |
| `\|10` | `expected chomping or indentation indicators, but found '0'` (col of the 2nd digit) |
| `\|--` | `expected chomping or indentation indicators, but found '-'` |
| `\|x`, `>x` | `expected chomping or indentation indicators, but found 'x'` |
| `\| x` | `expected a comment or a line break, but found 'x'` |
| `\| # c` | **OK** (comment allowed) |

### 9.1 Content indent
```
minIndent = max(1, scannerIndent + 1)
if (explicit n) contentIndent = minIndent + n - 1      // == scannerIndent + n  (n>=1)
else            contentIndent = max(minIndent, maxLeadingSpacesOfLeadingBlankRun)
```
`maxLeadingSpacesOfLeadingBlankRun` is obtained by consuming the run of spaces
and line breaks immediately after the header, tracking the deepest column
reached. **This means the auto-detected indent is the indentation of the FIRST
non-empty line, even if a later line is less indented — the block then simply
ends there.**

| input | value / result | why |
|---|---|---|
| `a: \|2<NL>··x<NL>···y<NL>` | `"x\n y\n"` | scannerIndent 0 → indent 2 |
| `a:<NL>··b: \|2<NL>····x<NL>·····y<NL>` | `"x\n y\n"` | scannerIndent 2 → indent 4 (**relative!**) |
| `\|2<NL>··x<NL>···y<NL>` (root) | `"x\n y\n"` | scannerIndent −1 → minIndent 1 → indent 2 |
| `- \|1<NL>·x<NL>` | `"x\n"` | scannerIndent 0 → indent 1 |
| `a: \|1<NL>····x<NL>` | `"···x\n"` | extra 3 spaces are content |
| `a: \|4<NL>··x<NL>` | ERROR `expected <block end>, but found '<scalar>'` (2:3) | content is shallower than the declared indent → empty block, then a stray scalar |
| `a: \|<NL>····x<NL>··y<NL>` | ERROR `expected <block end>, but found '<scalar>'` (3:3) | auto indent = 4, `  y` ends the block |
| `a: \|<NL>··x<NL>·y<NL>` | ERROR (3:2) | same |
| `a: \|<NL>······x<NL>······y<NL>` | `"x\ny\n"` | auto indent = 6 |

### 9.2 Line handling
For each content line, exactly `contentIndent` leading spaces are removed; any
remaining leading spaces are content. A line with **fewer** spaces than
`contentIndent` and nothing else is an *empty line* (contributes a break).

| input | value |
|---|---|
| `a: \|<NL>··x<NL>·<NL>··y<NL>` | `"x\n\ny\n"` (1-space line < indent → empty line) |
| `a: \|<NL>··x<NL>·····<NL>··y<NL>` | `"x\n···\ny\n"` (5-space line → 3 spaces of content) |
| `a: \|<NL>··x··<NL>··y<NL>` | `"x··\ny\n"` (trailing spaces kept) |
| `a: \|<NL><NL><NL>··x<NL>` | `"\n\nx\n"` (leading blank lines) |

### 9.3 Folding (`>`)
The break after line *L* becomes a single `<SP>` **only if** all of:
the break was `\n`-equivalent, *L* started with a non-space/non-tab char, the
**next** line starts with a non-space/non-tab char, and there is no blank line
between them. Otherwise the break is kept as `\n`.
**Trailing spaces are NOT stripped before folding** (PyYAML deviation):

| input | value |
|---|---|
| `a: ><NL>··x<NL>··y<NL>` | `"x y\n"` |
| `a: ><NL>··x··<NL>··y<NL>` | `"x···y\n"` ← three spaces (`"x  "` + fold space + `"y"`) |
| `a: ><NL>··x<NL><NL>··y<NL>` | `"x\ny\n"` |
| `a: ><NL>··x<NL><NL><NL>··y<NL>` | `"x\n\ny\n"` |
| `a: ><NL>··x<NL>····y<NL>··z<NL>` | `"x\n··y\nz\n"` (more-indented lines are not folded, and the break *before* them is kept) |
| `a: ><NL>··x<NL><NL>···y<NL>` | `"x\n\n·y\n"` |
| `a: ><NL>··x<NL>·····<NL>··y<NL>` | `"x\n···\ny\n"` |
| `a: ><NL>···x<NL>··y<NL>` | ERROR (auto indent 3, `  y` ends the block) |

### 9.4 Chomping
Let `T` = the line break that ended the last content line (`''` at EOF) and
`B` = the run of trailing empty-line breaks.
* clip (default): value + `T`
* strip (`-`): value only
* keep (`+`): value + `T` + `B`

| input | clip `\|` | strip `\|-` | keep `\|+` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `··x<NL>` | `"x\n"` | `"x"` | `"x\n"` |
| `··x<NL><NL><NL>` | `"x\n"` | `"x"` | `"x\n\n\n"` |
| `··x` (no final break) | `"x"` | `"x"` | `"x"` |
| (nothing) | `""` | `""` | `""` |
| `<NL>` only after header | `""` | `""` | `"\n"` |
| `<NL><NL>` only | `""` | `""` | `"\n\n"` |
| `>+ ··x<NL>··y<NL><NL>` | — | — | `"x y\n\n"` |
| `>- ··x<NL>···y<NL>··z<NL>` | — | `"x\n·y\nz"` | — |

### 9.5 Misc
* Block scalars are legal as a mapping value, a sequence item, and an explicit
  key (`? \|<NL>  x<NL>: v`).
* They are **illegal in flow context** (`[|` → "cannot start any token").
* `a: \|<NL>  x<NL>---<NL>` → the `---` at col 0 ends the block *and* starts a
  second document → `ComposerError … but found another document`.
* `---`, `...`, `#`, `{}`, `[]` inside the body are plain text.

---

## 10. Anchors, aliases, tags

### 10.1 Anchor / alias names
Name chars: `[0-9A-Za-z_-]+` (at least one). The character following the name
must be one of `\0 <SP> <TAB> <NL> <CR> <NEL> <LS> <PS> ? : , ] } % @ `` ` ``.
Anything else → `ScannerError: while scanning an anchor / expected alphabetic or
numeric character, but found '<c>'` (e.g. `&x.y`). `& ` / `* ` (empty name) →
same error with `' '`.

### 10.2 Semantics
| input | result |
|---|---|
| `a: &x 1<NL>b: *x` | `{a: 1, b: 1}` |
| `a: &x [1,2]<NL>b: *x` | the **same list object** twice → dumped as `a: &id001<NL>- 1<NL>- 2<NL>b: *id001` |
| `&x [ *x, {self: *x} ]` | recursive list → `--- &id001<NL>- *id001<NL>- self: *id001` |
| `&a {b: *a}` | recursive map → `--- &id001<NL>b: *id001` |
| `&k key: value` | anchor on the key node; output has no anchor (scalar not shared) |
| `a: &x k<NL>*x : v` | `{a: k, k: v}` (alias used as a key) |
| `{&k a: 1, *k : 2}` | key `a` twice → `{a: 2}` |
| `a: &foo<NL>b: 1` | anchor on an **empty node** → `{a: null, b: 1}` |
| `&k: 2` | `{null: 2}` |
| `a: &x 1<NL>b: &x 2` | `ComposerError: found duplicate anchor 'x'; first occurrence … second occurrence …` |
| `a: *x` (undefined) | `ComposerError: found undefined alias 'x'` |
| `a: &x 1<NL>b: *x y` | `ParserError: expected <block end>, but found '<scalar>'` |
| `a: &x,y z` | anchor `x`, then `,` → `ParserError: expected <block end>, but found ','` |
| `a: !!str &x 1` / `a: &x !!str 1` | both orders accepted |
| Emitted anchor names | `&id001`, `&id002`, … assigned in first-visit order over *shared/recursive* nodes only |

### 10.3 Tags
Forms: `!` (non-specific), `!local`, `!!suffix` (= `tag:yaml.org,2002:suffix`),
`!handle!suffix` (needs `%TAG`), `!<verbatim-uri>`. `%XX` percent-escapes are
decoded in the URI (`!%21` → tag `!!`).

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `a: !!str 42` | `{a: "42"}` (dumped `'42'`) |
| `a: !!int '7'` | `7` |
| `a: !!float '1.5'` | `1.5` |
| `a: !!bool 'yes'` | `true` |
| `a: !!null ''` | `null` |
| `a: !!timestamp 2001-12-14` | `datetime.date` → dumped `2001-12-14` |
| `a: !!map {x: 1}` / `!!seq [1]` | plain map/seq |
| `c: !!set {p, q}` | Python `set` → dumped `c: !!set<NL>··p: null<NL>··q: null` |
| `!!omap [{a: 1},{b: 2}]` | list of **tuples** → dumped with `!!python/tuple` |
| `d: !!binary aGVsbG8=` | `bytes` → dumped `d: !!binary \|<NL>··aGVsbG8=` |
| `!!binary 'not base64!!!'` | `ConstructorError: failed to decode base64 data: …` |
| `a: !<tag:yaml.org,2002:str> 42` | `"42"` |
| `a: ! 1` / `b: ! [1]` | non-specific tag → resolved as **str/plain default**: `! 1` → `1`?→ actually `{a: 1}` (int), `! [1]` → `[1]` |
| `a: !!str` (tag, no node) | `{a: ""}` |
| `a: !!foo bar` | `ConstructorError: could not determine a constructor for the tag 'tag:yaml.org,2002:foo'` |
| `a: !foo bar` | `ConstructorError: … for the tag '!foo'` |
| `a: !!python/tuple [1,2]` | `ConstructorError: … 'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/tuple'` (safe_load) |
| `a: !!str {b: 1}` | `ConstructorError: expected a scalar node, but found mapping` |
| `a: !!int [1]` | `expected a scalar node, but found sequence` |
| `a: !!map x` | `expected a mapping node, but found scalar` |
| `a: !!seq x` | `expected a sequence node, but found scalar` |
| `!!` (no suffix) | `ScannerError: expected URI, but found '\n'` |
| `!<>` | `ScannerError: expected URI, but found '>'` |
| `!<!foo> x` | tag `!foo` → constructor error |

### 10.4 Merge key `<<`
`<<` merges an alias-to-mapping (or a sequence of them) into the current
mapping. Explicit keys in the mapping win; with a list `[*x, *y]`, earlier
entries win over later ones.

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `a: &x {p: 1}<NL>b:<NL>  <<: *x<NL>  q: 2` | `b == {p:1, q:2}` |
| `<<: [*x, *y]` + `p: 9` (x={p:1}, y={r:3}) | `{p:9, r:3}` |
| two `<<:` keys in one mapping | both merged |
| `<<: 1` / `<<: *scalarAnchor` | `ConstructorError: while constructing a mapping … expected a mapping or list of mappings for merging, but found scalar` |

---

## 11. Documents, directives, explicit keys

### 11.1 Document markers
| input | result |
|---|---|
| `` (empty) | `--- null<NL>...<NL>` |
| `   <NL><NL>` | `--- null<NL>...<NL>` |
| `# a<NL># b<NL>` | `--- null<NL>...<NL>` |
| `--- foo<NL>` | `--- foo<NL>...<NL>` |
| `---<NL>a: 1<NL>` | normal map |
| `---<SP><SP><SP><NL>a: 1<NL>` | normal map |
| `--- # c<NL>a: 1<NL>` | normal map |
| `--- 1<NL>...<NL>` | `--- 1<NL>...<NL>` |
| `a: 1<NL>...<NL>` | `{a:1}` — a lone `...` just ends the document |
| `...<NL>` | `ParserError: while parsing a block node / expected the node content, but found '<document end>'` (1:1) |
| `a: 1<NL>...<NL>b: 2<NL>` | `ParserError: expected '<document start>', but found '<block mapping start>'` (3:1) |
| `a: 1<NL>...<NL>... x<NL>` | `ParserError: expected '<document start>', but found '<scalar>'` |
| `a: 1<NL>---<NL>b: 2<NL>` | `ComposerError: expected a single document in the stream … but found another document` (2:1) |
| `--- a<NL>--- b<NL>` | same ComposerError (2:1) |
| `a: ...` / `a: ---` | plain scalars `'...'` / `'---'` (only col-0 markers count) |
| `----<NL>` | RC=2 (argparse; see §0) |

`---` is only a marker at column 0 followed by space/break/EOF. Same for `...`.

### 11.2 Directives
| input | result |
|---|---|
| `%YAML 1.1<NL>---<NL>a: 010<NL>b: yes<NL>c: 0o17<NL>` | `{a: 8, b: true, c: "0o17"}` |
| `%YAML 1.2<NL>---<NL>` (same body) | **identical** — the declared version does **not** change resolution (always YAML-1.1-style resolver: `010`→8, `yes`→true, `0o17`→str) |
| `%YAML 2.0` / `%YAML 0.9` | `ParserError: found incompatible YAML document (version 1.* is required)` (1:1) |
| `%YAML 1` | `ScannerError: expected a digit or '.', but found '\n'` |
| `%YAML 1.1<NL>%YAML 1.1<NL>---<NL>…` | `ParserError: found duplicate YAML directive` (2:1) |
| `%YAML 1.1<NL>a: 1<NL>` (no `---`) | `ParserError: expected '<document start>', but found '<scalar>'` (2:1) |
| `%foo<NL>` alone | `ParserError: expected '<document start>', but found '<stream end>'` (2:1) |
| `%FOO bar<NL>---<NL>a: 1<NL>` | unknown directives are **ignored** → `{a:1}` |
| `%TAG !e! tag:yaml.org,2002:<NL>---<NL>!e!str 42<NL>` | `'42'` |
| `%TAG ! tag:example.com,2000:<NL>---<NL>!thing x<NL>` | tag `tag:example.com,2000:thing` → constructor error |
| `%TAG !! tag:example.com,2000:` | overrides the `!!` handle |
| `# c<NL>%YAML 1.1<NL>---<NL>a: 1` | comments before directives are fine |
| `---<NL>%TAG ! x:<NL>` | `ParserError: expected '<document start>', but found '<stream end>'` |
| `--- a: 1` after a directive | ERROR (§3, not directive-related) |

### 11.3 Explicit keys `?` / `:`
| input | result |
|---|---|
| `? a<NL>: b<NL>` | `{a: b}` |
| `? a<NL>` | `{a: null}` |
| `?<NL>: v<NL>` | `{null: v}` |
| `?<NL>:<NL>` | `{null: null}` |
| `? a<NL>: 1<NL>? b<NL>: 2<NL>` | `{a:1,b:2}` |
| `? a<NL>: 1<NL>b: 2<NL>` | `{a:1,b:2}` (mixing explicit and simple keys OK) |
| `?a: 1` | plain key `?a` |
| `: b<NL>` | `ParserError: while parsing a block mapping / expected <block end>, but found ':'` |
| `? [a, b]<NL>: c<NL>` | `ConstructorError: found unhashable key` (1:3) |
| `? {a: 1}<NL>: c` / `? - a<NL>  - b<NL>: c` | same unhashable-key error |
| `{a: 1}: v` / `[1,2]: v` | `ConstructorError: while constructing a mapping / found unhashable key` (1:1) |
| `- a<NL>: v<NL>` | `ParserError: expected <block end>, but found ':'` |
| `? \|<NL>  x<NL>: v<NL>` | `{"x\n": v}` |
| `? a<NL>: \|<NL>  x<NL>` | `{a: "x\n"}` |

Duplicate keys: last one wins (`a: 1<NL>a: 2` → `{a: 2}`), no warning.

---

## 12. Output framing (needed to reproduce stdout byte-exactly)

These belong to the emitter area but are unavoidable when replaying cases:

1. `explicit_start=True` → output always begins `---`. For a **collection** root
   it is `---<NL>` then the block; for a **scalar** root it is `--- <scalar>`.
   For an empty flow collection root it is `--- {}` / `--- []`.
2. A trailing `...<NL>` is emitted iff the document root was written as a
   **plain scalar** (`open_ended`). So `--- null<NL>...<NL>`, `--- foo<NL>...<NL>`,
   `--- 42<NL>...<NL>`, `--- one two three<NL>...<NL>` get `...`;
   but `--- 'x'`, `--- '42'`, `--- !!set …`, `--- {}`, `--- &id001 …`, and every
   collection root do **not**.
3. `print()` appends one more `<NL>`.
4. Mapping keys are **sorted** (`yaml.dump` default `sort_keys=True`); the sort
   is Python's `<` on the key objects (so all-string keys sort by codepoint;
   `?a` < `a` < `a#b`).
5. Block sequences nested directly under a mapping key are emitted
   **indentless** (`a:<NL>- 1`), matching the input form in §4.
6. A key is emitted as `? key<NL>: value` when it is empty, multi-line, or
   **≥128 characters** long.
7. Shared/recursive nodes get `&id001`, `&id002`, … in first-visit order.

---

## 13. OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **NUL byte** (`\x00`) in the input: unreachable through `argv` (Node and
   `execve` both refuse). The reader's printability regex would reject it
   (`unacceptable character #x0000`), but this could not be observed. Tried:
   `spawnSync` with `\0` in the argument → `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`.
2. **Lone surrogates** (`\uD800`–`\uDFFF`): cannot be encoded as valid UTF-8 in
   `argv`, so the `퟿`/`` boundary of the printability class was not
   observed directly. Inferred from the `￾`/`�` and `\x9F`/`\xA0`
   boundaries that the class is
   `\x09\x0A\x0D\x20-\x7E\x85\xA0-퟿-�\U00010000-\U0010FFFF`.
3. Exact interaction of `%TAG` handle shadowing with `!!` when the document also
   uses `!` was only spot-checked (`%TAG !! …` and `%TAG ! …` both take effect);
   the full handle-resolution table (e.g. re-declaring the same handle twice)
   was not probed.
4. The stderr `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` suffix number is nondeterministic, so stderr
   cannot be compared byte-for-byte; only RC and stdout can.
5. Tab handling inside a *folded* (`>`) block scalar where the tab is the first
   char after the indent (affects the `leading_non_space` fold test) was probed
   only for literal blocks (`|`), not `>`.

input.new_string:
4. Mapping keys are **sorted**, but with a Python-specific catch
   (`yaml.dump` default `sort_keys=True` does `try: items = sorted(items)
   except TypeError: pass`):
   * All keys mutually comparable → sorted by Python `<` on the `(key, value)`
     **tuples** (so equal keys tie-break on the value). All-string keys sort by
     codepoint: `?a` (0x3F) < `A` (0x41) < `a` < `a#b` < `z`. All-int keys sort
     numerically; ints and floats sort together (`1` < `1.5`).
   * Any pair of keys that Python refuses to compare (str vs int, str vs bool,
     str vs None, …) makes `sorted` raise `TypeError`, which is **swallowed** →
     that mapping keeps **insertion (document) order**. Verified:
     `a: 1<NL>1: 2` → `a: 1<NL>1: 2`; `true: 1<NL>a: 2` → `true: 1<NL>a: 2`;
     `~: 1<NL>a: 2` → `null: 1<NL>a: 2`. Decided **per mapping**, independently
     for nested mappings.

3. **`%TAG` handle shadowing:** `%TAG !! …` and `%TAG ! …` both take effect, and
   re-declaring the same handle raises `duplicate tag handle`. The full
   interaction of a redefined `!` handle with `!!`-shorthands in the same

5. Tab handling in a *folded* (`>`) block scalar was verified after this spec was
   first written: a TAB immediately after the stripped indent sets
   `leadingNonSpace = false`, and a next line starting with TAB also blocks the
   fold. `a: ><NL>··x<NL>··<TAB>y<NL>` → `"x\n\ty\n"`;
   `a: ><NL>··<TAB>x<NL>··y<NL>` → `"\tx\ny\n"`. No open question remains here.
6. Whether `sorted()` on a mapping can *partially* succeed (it cannot — Python's
   sort either completes or raises, and the pre-sort list is left untouched) was
   only inferred, not directly forced with an adversarial comparison ordering.

7	Everything below is from black-box observation. Case files live in

9	spec is `/workspace/dev/_sp/rec.txt` (regenerate with

11	
12	Notation: `<SP>`/`·` = space, `<TAB>`, `<NL>` = LF, `<CR>`, `<NEL>` = U+0085,
13	`<LS>` = U+2028, `<PS>` = U+2029, `<BOM>` = U+FEFF, `<NBSP>` = U+00A0.

16	
17	## 0. Harness / process-level facts (read first)
18	
19	| fact | detail |
20	|---|---|
21	| success | exit code **0**, result on stdout, stderr empty |
22	| any YAML error | exit code **1**, **stdout empty**, Python traceback on stderr |
23	| stderr last line | `[PYI-<n>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test9' due to unhandled exception!` where `<n>` **varies run to run** → stderr is *not* byte-reproducible. Only RC + stdout are. |
24	| `print()` | adds one extra `<NL>` after `yaml.dump`'s output, so every successful stdout ends with `\n\n` (dump already ends with `\n`) |
25	| argparse quirk | the value is passed as `["--a", value]`. `argparse` treats a token as an option if it starts with `-` **and contains no ASCII space**. So `---`, `----`, `-`, `-\n-\n-\n` → **RC=2**, `usage: ...` + `error: argument --a: expected one argument`. Values that start with `-` but contain a space (e.g. `- 1\n- 2`, `--- foo`) are fine. |
26	| NUL | `\x00` cannot be passed through `argv` at all (OS/execve limit). Untestable — **OPEN QUESTION** (see §12). |
27	
28	Error-message shape (when you want to reproduce stderr text, ignore the PYI line):
29	
30	```
31	yaml.<module>.<Class>Error: <context>            <- optional context line
32	  in "<unicode string>", line L, column C:
33	    <snippet of that line>
34	    <caret>
35	<problem>                                        <- always present
36	  in "<unicode string>", line L2, column C2:
37	    <snippet>
38	    <caret>
39	```
40	`line`/`column` are **1-based**. Snippets are indented 4 spaces and elided with
41	` ... ` when the line is long (see case 99/100). `ReaderError` uses
42	`in "<unicode string>", position N` with a **0-based codepoint index** instead.
43

## 13. OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **NUL byte** (`\x00`) in the input: unreachable through `argv` (Node and
   `execve` both refuse). The reader's printability regex would reject it
   (`unacceptable character #x0000`), but this could not be observed. Tried:
   `spawnSync` with `\0` in the argument → `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`.
2. **Lone surrogates** (`\uD800`–`\uDFFF`): cannot be encoded as valid UTF-8 in
   `argv`, so the `\uD7FF`/`\uE000` boundary of the printability class was not
   observed directly. Inferred from the `￾`/`�` and `\x9F`/`\xA0`
   boundaries that the class is
   `[\t\n\r\x20-\x7E\x85\xA0-\uD7FF\uE000-\uFFFD\u{10000}-\u{10FFFF}]`.
3. **`%TAG` handle shadowing:** `%TAG !! …` and `%TAG ! …` both take effect, and
   re-declaring the same handle raises `duplicate tag handle`. The full
   interaction of a redefined `!` handle with `!!`-shorthands in the same
   document was not exhaustively probed.
4. The stderr `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` suffix number is nondeterministic, so stderr
   cannot be compared byte-for-byte; only RC and stdout can.
5. Tab handling in a *folded* (`>`) block scalar was verified after this spec was
   first written: a TAB immediately after the stripped indent sets
   `leadingNonSpace = false`, and a next line starting with TAB also blocks the
   fold. `a: ><NL>··x<NL>··<TAB>y<NL>` → `"x\n\ty\n"`;
   `a: ><NL>··<TAB>x<NL>··y<NL>` → `"\tx\ny\n"`. No open question remains here.
6. Whether `sorted()` on a mapping can *partially* succeed (it cannot — Python's
   sort either completes or raises, and the pre-sort list is left untouched) was
   only inferred, not directly forced with an adversarial comparison ordering.

   observed directly. Inferred from the `￾`/`�` and `\x9F`/`\xA0`
   boundaries that the class is
   `[\t\n\r\x20-\x7E\x85\xA0-\uD7FF\uE000-\uFFFD\u{10000}-\u{10FFFF}]`.
3. **`%TAG` handle shadowing:** `%TAG !! …` and `%TAG ! …` both take effect, and
   re-declaring the same handle raises `duplicate tag handle`. The full
   interaction of a redefined `!` handle with `!!`-shorthands in the same
   document was not exhaustively probed.
4. The stderr `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` suffix number is nondeterministic, so stderr
   cannot be compared byte-for-byte; only RC and stdout can.
5. Whether `sorted()` on a mapping can *partially* succeed (it cannot — Python's
   sort either completes or raises, and the pre-sort list is left untouched) was
   only inferred, not directly forced with an adversarial comparison ordering.
===

RULES ESTABLISHED — YAML scanning/parsing for `test9_executable`

MOST SURPRISING / NON-OBVIOUS
1. **TABs are fatal almost everywhere.** `scan_to_next_token` skips only `' '`. Any TAB where a token could start → `ScannerError: found character '\t' that cannot start any token`. That includes `a:<TAB>b`, `a: b<TAB>c`, a *trailing* `a: 1<TAB>`, TAB before a `#`, TAB as indentation, TAB after a comma in flow, and a TAB-only line inside a `|` block (which ends the block, then errors). TABs are legal only inside `'…'`, `"…"`, and block-scalar bodies after the indent is stripped.
2. **`%YAML 1.2` changes nothing.** `010`→8, `yes`→true, `0o17`→str under both 1.1 and 1.2. `%YAML 2.0`/`0.9` → `ParserError: found incompatible YAML document (version 1.* is required)`. Unknown directives (`%FOO`) are silently ignored. A directive with no `---` → `expected '<document start>'`.
3. **Key sorting silently degrades to insertion order.** `yaml.dump` does `try: sorted(items) except TypeError: pass`. All-comparable keys → sorted by Python `<` on `(key, value)` tuples (`?a` < `A` < `a` < `a#b`). Any str/int, str/bool, str/None mix → **document order preserved**, decided per mapping.
4. **`--- a: 1` is an ERROR** (`mapping values are not allowed here`), and `--- - a` is `sequence entries are not allowed here`, because `---` sets `allowSimpleKey = false`. But `--- foo`, `--- {a:1}`, `--- [1,2]`, `--- |`, `--- &a 1`, `--- !!str 1` all work.
5. **Non-specific tag `!` forces implicit resolution regardless of style**: `! 1`→int 1, `! yes`→true, **`! '1'`→int 1**.
6. **`>` does NOT strip trailing spaces before folding**: `>` over `"  x  " / "  y"` yields `"x   y\n"` (3 spaces).
7. **A block scalar's explicit indent indicator is RELATIVE to the enclosing block indent**: `contentIndent = scannerIndent + n` (root: `scannerIndent = -1` → `contentIndent = n`). `a:\n  b: |2` → indent 4, not 2. `|0` → `expected indentation indicator in the range 1-9`; `|10` and `|--` → `expected chomping or indentation indicators`. `|2-` and `|-2` both legal.
8. **Auto-detected block indent = indentation of the FIRST non-empty line.** `a: |\n    x\n  y` errors (indent 4; `  y` ends the block, then `expected <block end>, but found '<scalar>'`). Same for `|4` with 2-space content.
9. **U+2028/U+2029 are line breaks but are NOT normalised** — they survive verbatim into scalars (`a: x<LS>  y` → `"x\u2028y"`), whereas `\r`, `\r\n`, and **U+0085 (NEL)** all normalise to `\n` and fold to a space.
10. **BOM does not advance the column counter**, and only a BOM at index 0 is stripped; elsewhere it is scalar content (`a:\n ﻿ b: 1` → key `"\uFEFF b"` at indent 1).
11. **Simple-key limit is exactly `index - keyStart > 1024`.** Block key of 1024 `k` OK, 1025 → `mapping values are not allowed here` at col 1026. In flow, `{`+1024 OK (span counts from after `{`), 1030 → `expected ',' or '}', but got ':'`. Quotes count toward the span.
12. **"required simple key" produces a weird error.** If a discarded stale key sat at `column == current block indent`, you get `while scanning a simple key … could not find expected ':'` pointing at EOF. Hits `a:\n1`, `a:\n  b: one\n  two`, `a: one\n---- x`, `a\nb: 1`.
13. **Reader-level printability check runs on the whole string before parsing**: class `[\t\n\r\x20-\x7E\x85\xA0-\uD7FF\uE000-\uFFFD\u{10000}-\u{10FFFF}]`; first violation → `ReaderError: unacceptable character #xNNNN … position N` (**0-based codepoint index**). `\x0B`/`\x0C` are rejected as raw bytes even though `\v`/`\f` are valid escapes.

REST OF THE MODEL (condensed)
14. `allowSimpleKey` state machine drives most errors: set true at stream start / after a block-context line break / after `[ { , - |` `>`; set false after `%dir`, `---`, `...`, `] }`, `:`, `& * !`, quoted, plain. `-`/`?`/`:` with it false → `sequence entries` / `mapping keys` / `mapping values are not allowed here`.
15. `:` ends a plain scalar iff followed by space/TAB/break/EOF, plus (flow only) `, [ ] { }`. In flow a plain scalar also ends at any of `, ? [ ] { }`. So `a:b` is one scalar, `[a:]`→`[{a:null}]`, `{a: b:}` errors, `a:: 1`→key `a:`.
16. Cannot start a plain scalar: `, [ ] { }` → `expected the node content, but found '<c>'`; `@ ` `` ` `` `%` → `cannot start any token`. All are fine mid-scalar.
17. Plain folding: 1 break → `' '`; n blank lines → n `\n`; internal space runs preserved verbatim; trailing spaces dropped. Continuation needs `column >= blockIndent + 1` (root indent −1 → col 0 OK). A col-0 `---`/`...` (followed by space/break/EOF) terminates it; 4 dashes do not.
18. `#` is a comment only at token start or after ≥1 space; `a#b` and `b#c` stay literal. A comment on a plain-scalar continuation line terminates the scalar.
19. Double-quoted escapes accepted: `\0 \a \b \t \<TAB> \n \v \f \r \e \" \\ \/ \<SP> \N \_ \L \P \xHH \uHHHH \UHHHHHHHH`; `\<NL>` = continuation dropping the break and the next line's leading whitespace. Bad escape → `found unknown escape character 'q'`; short hex → `expected escape sequence of N hexadecimal numbers`.
20. Chomping: clip = value + last break; strip = value; keep = value + last break + trailing empty-line breaks. **No final break in the input → all three give the same result** (`|+\n  x` → `"x"`). A block line with fewer spaces than the indent is an empty line; with more, the extras are content.
21. Flow: trailing commas fine; `[1, , 2]` / `[,]` / `{,}` error; `{a: , b, d:}` gives nulls; `?` works in flow mappings and `[? a]`→`[{a:null}]`; block indicators (`-`, `|`) inside flow error.
22. Indentless sequences under a mapping key are allowed, but only relative to their **own** parent key (`a:\n  b:\n- 1` errors with `expected <block end>, but found '-'`).
23. Anchors: name `[0-9A-Za-z_-]+`, must be followed by one of `\0 SP TAB break ? : , ] } % @ ` `` ` ``; `&x.y` → `expected alphabetic or numeric character`. Duplicate anchor → `found duplicate anchor 'x'; first/second occurrence`. Aliasing a collection yields the **same object** (dumped `&id001`/`*id001`); recursion works. Anchor on an empty node → null. `<<` merge works, incl. `[*x,*y]` (earlier wins, explicit keys win); non-map → `expected a mapping or list of mappings for merging`.
24. Tags: `!!foo`, `!local`, `!!python/*` → `ConstructorError: could not determine a constructor for the tag '…'`; wrong kind → `expected a scalar/mapping/sequence node, but found …`; `%XX` decoded in tag URIs; `!!` alone → `expected URI`; duplicate `%TAG` handle → `duplicate tag handle`.
25. Documents: two documents → `ComposerError: expected a single document in the stream … but found another document`; content after `...` → `expected '<document start>'`; bare `...` → `expected the node content, but found '<document end>'`; empty/whitespace/comment-only input → `--- null\n...\n`.
26. Output framing needed for replay: `---` always; `--- <scalar>` for scalar roots; trailing `...` **only** when the root was written as a plain scalar; `print()` adds one extra newline; keys ≥128 chars / empty / multi-line are emitted as `? k\n: v`.
27. Process contract: success RC=0; any YAML error RC=1 with **empty stdout**; stderr ends with a nondeterministic `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` line, so only RC + stdout are byte-comparable. Values starting with `-` and containing no ASCII space (e.g. `---`, `-`) are rejected by argparse with RC=2 before YAML ever runs.

Spec: `/workspace/dev/spec/scanner-parser.md` (690 lines). Cases: `/workspace/dev/cases/scanner-parser/01..123-*.txt` (68 success, 55 error, all verified deterministic and none hitting argparse RC=2). Replay recorder: `/workspace/dev/_sp/record.js`, captured output `/workspace/dev/_sp/rec2.txt`.
